subject: Fintonic: sustained queue-depth spike — reserved throughput gap & exec ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintonic.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Feb 20, 2028 at 08:15 AM PST
Subject: Fintonic: sustained queue-depth spike — reserved throughput gap & exec ask

Hi Priya — looping you and ops in. We’re seeing an elevated queue depth on the reserved capacity pool backing your production models since ~04:00 PST this morning. Symptoms we’ve observed: sustained 95th-percentile latency increases to ~1.8s (baseline 350ms), a spike in 429 throttles, and a small uptick in inference errors for longer sequences. I attached a short window of the raw metrics (throughput_window_20280220.csv) and a handful of error traces.

Quick summary of impact:
- Customer-facing requests are intermittently hitting throttles which manifests as retries on your side.
- Tail latency is ~5x higher than your SLA target for a small but consistent fraction of requests.

Immediate asks:
1) Can we stand up an exec bridge within the hour so we can align on customer messaging and an interim capacity move?
2) Approve a temporary reserved-capacity slide (re-route 2x reserved units) from our non-critical pools to Fintonic while we investigate root cause. This is a manual action that requires Marissa or Marcus to greenlight.

I’ll paste a short timeline and current mitigation notes in follow-ups.

—Naomi
Head of Account Success, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Impact from Fintonic:
- Approx 120 affected sessions in the last hour, most for batch inference (larger payloads).
- Several enterprise customers seeing retries which amplifies load.

Priya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Feb 20, 2028 at 09:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Fintonic: sustained queue-depth spike — reserved throughput gap & exec ask

Quick infra note — preliminary observations from the serving layer:
- We’ve got sustained headroom drain on the fintonic-reserved pool  (pool id: rsv-fin-4821) starting 03:50 PST.
- Root signal: a recent model rollout from a 3rd-party partner increased mean token-generation time by ~2.3x for a subset of requests; combined with larger-than-expected client batch sizes this amplified queueing.
- Autoscaler did not trigger new GPUs because the allocation policy favored latency SLOs in the hosting pool and the reserved pool config has a conservative burst policy.

Immediate mitigations I’m proposing now:
1) Manual provisional capacity reassign: move two reserved workers (GPU nodes) from pool rsv-dataprep to rsv-fin-4821. This will reduce queue depth in ~6 minutes.
2) Temporarily enforce a client-side batch cap for Fintonic (we can push a short-lived policy at the routing layer).
3) Start longer-term: widen reserved pool burst window and adjust autoscaler thresholds for reserved tenants.

I can execute 1) with Marissa approval. Jonas and infra team stand by to flip the routing cap once approved.

—Marcus
Director, Serving Infrastructure
[attachment: throughput_window_20280220.csv (csv)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Feb 20, 2028 at 09:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Fintonic: sustained queue-depth spike — reserved throughput gap & exec ask

Status update from ops:
- I’ve queued the manual node reassignment; it requires Marissa to confirm because the donors are from a dedicated business-critical pool. If approved I expect queue depth to fall within 8 minutes and user-facing 429s to drop substantially in ~10-12 minutes after reroute.
- I’m also enabling a temporary KV-cache TTL bump for the Fintonic model family to reduce repeated prefix work.
- ETA for a deeper root-cause fix (config + autoscaler changes + partner rollback if needed): 36-48 hours.

I’ll join the exec bridge and provide live metrics.

—Jonas
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: fintonic-impact-note-draft.md (md)]

Date: Tue, Feb 20, 2028 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: EXTERNAL: Exec attention requested — Fintonic impact summary and proposed customer remedy

Marissa — reiterating the ask: we need signoff to move two reserved workers to Fintonic immediately and sign off on a short-term SLA credit should the customer request it. The customer is already seeing visible user impact and we should be proactive with a conciliatory credit to limit churn risk.

Draft talking points for the exec bridge (I’ll host at 10:30 PT):
- What happened: queue-depth spike due to partner model rollout + larger batch sizes, causing reserved pool headroom drain.
- What we’re doing now: manual capacity shift (2 nodes), routing-level batch cap, KV-cache TTL bump. Expected user-visible improvement in ~10-12 minutes.
- Next steps: autoscaler and reserved-pool tuning (36-48h window), request partner rollback if regression persists.
- Compensation ask: propose a one-month service credit on Fintonic’s next bill if impact exceeds SLA thresholds.

Please confirm ASAP so Jonas can proceed with the reassignment and I can brief Fintonic on the timeline.

—Naomi
